purpose: Offline evaluation evidence only. This file must not be used as collector seeds, queries, runtime fixtures, or event imports.
selection_method: Ten distinct Philippine community/student competitions were selected through independent web research without reading collector outputs, retained reports, or runtime source configuration. Generic searches identified publishers and events; event-name follow-up searches verified already independently identified candidates. The supplied acceptance case is separate and excluded from the ten-event denominator.
initial_discovery_queries: Philippines cybersecurity community capture the flag registration competition university
Philippines CTF competition student cybersecurity registration community
personal_profile_research_queries: Philippine community CTF competition personal Facebook announcement
limitations: This is a small convenience benchmark of independently documented competitions, not a random or representative coverage estimate.

No additional original personal-profile Facebook announcements, or proof they were the first announcement, were independently established. The supplied RAIJIN case cannot establish coverage across several personal-profile organizers.
Original Facebook identities are unknown for all ten benchmark events. Absence of an identified original is not evidence that Facebook was unused.
Several sources are recaps. They prove event existence and Philippine scope but cannot establish an advance registration opportunity.
A publication date is not a collector first-seen timestamp. Timeliness requires actual collector observations plus registration evidence.
Research results are distinct from daily collector results. All normal-run measurement fields are initially null for evaluation by the root agent.

AdU Hackademic Showdown is supported by indexed campus-newsletter content on a third-party PDF host. The publisher account/ownership was not independently confirmed; it is weaker provenance than a first-party university article.
